title: Consumer rights
examples: What should I do if I buy something that breaks quickly?
Do I always get my money back for something?
Where can I find out about my consumer rights?

explain.say: Today we are learning about consumer rights in your country.

items: Know your rights when buying things.
Understand what to do if things go wrong.
Learn about getting your money back.

explain.say: First we will look at getting refunds for items you return.

items: Step 1: Check the store's return policy.
Step 2: Keep your proof of purchase.
Step 3: Return the item within the time limit.

explain.say: If you return an item, you usually need your receipt or proof of purchase.
Next we learn about faulty goods, which are items that do not work correctly.
If goods are faulty, you generally have the right to a repair or a full refund.
In real life, if you buy a toaster that only toasts one side, it is faulty.

faq.q: Do I always get my money back if I change my mind?
faq.a: Not necessarily; most stores have a specific return policy you must follow. You might only get store credit instead of cash.
asks: Can I return it just because I don't like it?
Is there a cooling-off period for returns?

faq.a: A faulty good is one that does not work as advertised or is damaged upon arrival. It means it is not fit for its intended purpose.
asks: If it breaks next week, is it faulty?
Does it have to be broken right away to be faulty?

faq.q: What proof do I need when I return something?
faq.a: The best proof is the original receipt or a bank statement showing the purchase. Always check what the shop requires.
asks: Can I use a photo of the receipt?
Do I need the original packaging?

faq.q: What if the store refuses to take it back?
faq.a: You should ask to speak to a manager or look up your local consumer protection agency. They can advise you on your rights.
asks: Who can I call if the shop argues with me?
Is there a government body that helps with this?

faq.q: Does the law cover online purchases too?
faq.a: Yes, consumer rights laws usually apply to online sales as well. The seller must still meet the standards of quality and function.
asks: Do I get the same rights buying online?

facts: Consumer rights protect buyers from unfair trade practices.
Keeping proof of purchase, like a receipt, is very important.
If goods are faulty, you usually have the right to repair or refund.
Store return policies vary, so always read the terms and conditions.

quiz.say: You buy a jacket, but the zipper breaks after one week of use. According to consumer rights, what is your best initial action?
quiz.show: A. Buy a new jacket immediately.

options.show: Return it to the store for repair or refund.
options.say: Return it to the store for repair or refund.

options.show: A. Wait until it breaks completely.
options.say: A. Wait until it breaks completely.

options.show: B. Try to fix it yourself with glue.
options.say: B. Try to fix it yourself with glue.

options.show: C. Just buy a different jacket.
options.say: C. Just buy a different jacket.

quiz.why: Because the zipper breaking means the jacket is faulty, you have rights regarding repair or replacement.

wrong.1: Waiting too long might make the store argue that the fault was caused by you.
wrong.2: While you can try, the store might refuse the refund if you have damaged it further.
wrong.3: This ignores your right to remedy for the faulty item you already bought.

quiz.say: A shop says they only accept returns within 14 days, but you bought the item 10 days ago and it is faulty. What should you do?
quiz.show: A. Point out the fault first.

options.show: B. Leave the shop because of the rule.
options.say: B. Leave the shop because of the rule.

options.show: C. Blame the shop for the fault.
options.say: C. Blame the shop for the fault.

options.show: Focus on the fault rather than the return date.
options.say: Focus on the fault rather than the return date.

quiz.why: Faulty goods rights are often separate from simple change-of-mind return periods.

wrong.0: Leaving without speaking to a manager means you give up your right to challenge the rule.
wrong.1: While true, you must still follow the proper procedure to get your money back.
wrong.3: This ignores the fact that the item is physically broken, which is a legal issue.

quiz.say: If you buy a book online, and it arrives with pages missing, what is the primary consumer right you are relying on?
quiz.show: A. Right to a refund for poor quality.

options.show: C. Right to an exchange for a new book.
options.say: C. Right to an exchange for a new book.

options.show: Right to a refund for faulty goods.
options.say: Right to a refund for faulty goods.

options.show: A. Right to a refund for poor quality.
options.say: A. Right to a refund for poor quality.

options.show: B. Right to a refund for late delivery.
options.say: B. Right to a refund for late delivery.

quiz.why: Missing pages mean the book is not complete or as advertised, making it faulty.

wrong.0: While possible, the right to a refund is often the most straightforward remedy for missing parts.
wrong.2: This is too general; the missing pages make it faulty, which is more specific.
wrong.3: The issue here is the condition of the book, not when it arrived.
